findings.title: require_admin condition is always false
findings.description: The check `session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"` is always true for any role, so admin access is never granted (and the function always errors). The operands should be combined with `&&`.

findings.title: verify accepts expired sessions
findings.description: verify only compares tokens and never consults Session::expires_at, so tokens keep working indefinitely past their 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: bearer_token panics on malformed Authorization header
findings.description: Indexing parts[1] panics when the header has fewer than two whitespace-separated tokens (e.g. missing or malformed header), killing the handler thread instead of producing a clean 401.

findings.title: utilization percentage is wrong due to integer division
findings.description: Computing `guard.len() / self.limit * 100` divides first, yielding 0 for any partial cache and 100 only when full. The dashboard percentage is therefore always 0 or 100.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is treated as seconds
findings.description: The variable is documented as milliseconds and should build a Duration with from_millis, but the code calls from_secs(n), so a configured TTL is 1000x too long.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The parsed limit is discarded (only `_ = limit`), so cfg.fetch_limit always retains its default of 32 regardless of the environment.

findings.title: validate always returns Ok even for invalid config
findings.description: Problems are collected and printed but validate() returns Ok(()) unconditionally, so a bad deploy (invalid port, zero timeout) does not fail at startup as documented.

findings.title: create panics for any owner without an existing quota entry
findings.description: `self.quota.get_mut(owner).unwrap()` panics on the first link created by a new owner because no quota entry exists yet, making link creation unusable for new users.

findings.title: resolve condition is inverted, deleting live links
findings.description: expired is set to `now < expires_at` (i.e. still alive), then the link is removed when that is true, so every valid, unexpired link is deleted on first access while expired links are kept and counted.

findings.title: rename validates `from` twice and never validates `to`
findings.description: The second validate_code call checks `from` again instead of `to`, so an invalid destination code passes validation while a valid one is never checked.

findings.title: page() can slice out of bounds and panic
findings.description: When offset+size exceeds the number of links, end is set to `all.len() + 1`, and `all[offset..end]` then indexes past the end of the slice, panicking the handler.

findings.title: success_rate is always 0 unless every link has hits
findings.description: Integer division `used / self.links.len() * 100` evaluates to 0 for any partial usage because the division happens before the multiply.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending instead of descending
findings.description: The leaderboard is documented as most hits first but sorts with `a.hits.cmp(&b.hits)` (ascending), so the least-followed links are returned and the most-followed are truncated away.

findings.title: by_owner uses substring match instead of equality
findings.description: `l.owner.contains(owner)` returns links whose owner merely contains the query as a substring, leaking or misattributing data (e.g. owner "a" matches "alice").

findings.title: extend revives expired links despite documented finality
findings.description: extend unconditionally sets expires_at to now + ttl, even for already-expired links, contradicting the comment that an expired link stays expired and must never come back to life.

findings.title: quotas exposes a mutable reference, violating its snapshot contract
findings.description: quotas() returns `&mut HashMap`, allowing callers to mutate the store's internal quota map, contrary to the doc comment that counts are a snapshot.

findings.title: prune returns remaining count instead of removed count
findings.description: prune discards `before` and returns `self.links.len()`, but its documentation promises the number of links removed.

findings.title: expires_at panics on missing code
findings.description: Using `.unwrap()` on a missing code panics; callers (janitor included) may request unknown codes.

findings.title: stats divides by zero when store is empty
findings.description: `hits / guard.len() as i64` panics with division by zero on an empty store, reachable via GET /stats.

findings.title: Metrics::add_resolved is non-atomic
findings.description: Loading then storing loses concurrent updates under multiple threads, undercounting resolved links compared with add_created/add_error which use fetch_add.

findings.title: warm_cache returns before spawned probes finish
findings.description: The join handles are collected into a Vec and immediately dropped, so warm_cache does not wait as its documentation claims.

findings.title: count_by_owner double-locks the store (deadlock) and returns total link count
findings.description: The Mutex is not reentrant, so the second store.lock().unwrap() blocks forever; even if it did not, guard.len() is returned instead of a per-owner count, contradicting the function name.

findings.title: write_snapshot ignores rename failure and always succeeds
findings.description: `let _ = fs::rename(...)` discards the result, so the function returns Ok even when the atomic move (possibly across filesystems) fails, leaving no durable snapshot.

findings.title: archive_all ignores per-link write errors
findings.description: write! failures are discarded with `let _`, so truncated archives are reported as success.

findings.title: count_by_owner locks the same Mutex twice, deadlocking every caller
findings.description: The function takes store.lock() and never releases it before calling store.lock() again on the same std::sync::Mutex, which is not reentrant. The second acquisition blocks forever waiting for the first guard to drop, so any request path that invokes count_by_owner hangs indefinitely.

findings.title: Lock-order inversion between Cache::get/peek paths and Cache::flush
findings.description: get() acquires entries (RwLock) and then hits (Mutex), while flush() acquires hits first and then entries. Two threads taking the locks in opposite orders form a classic AB/BA deadlock, e.g. a request reading the cache concurrently with an admin Flush.

findings.title: Metrics::add_resolved loses updates under concurrency
findings.description: add_resolved does a non-atomic load then store, so two threads can both read the same value and both store value+1, losing one increment. add_created and add_error use fetch_add and do not have this problem, making the counters inconsistent under load.

findings.title: warm_cache never joins the spawned threads despite claiming to return after completion
findings.description: The function spawns one thread per pair, collects the JoinHandles, and then discards them with let _ = handles;. It returns before the probes finish, so callers observe a partially primed cache and the worker threads outlive the call and can leak.

findings.title: check_targets leaks worker threads and blocks them on the channel when it returns early
findings.description: The sync_channel has capacity 0, so a spawned probe's send blocks until a matching recv. When a failing target causes an early return from the receive loop, no one ever receives from the remaining senders, so those threads block on send forever and leak; repeated failing probes exhaust threads.

findings.title: Handlers hold the store mutex across network I/O and responses
findings.description: create_link, redirect, list_links, admin_quotas, stats and report keep the store guard alive while they call self.respond/redirect_to, which writes to the TCP stream and can block. The lock is held during slow network I/O, serializing all requests and risking request-thread pileup; store mutation is also interleaved with unrelated metric calls.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses a fixed /tmp tempfile, racing concurrent snapshots
findings.description: All callers use the same /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json path. Concurrent snapshot writes truncate each other's temporary file before the rename, so one writer's bytes can be mixed in or a snapshot can be lost, defeating the atomic-rename guarantee.

findings.title: Janitor thread is not reaped when JanitorStop is dropped without stop()
findings.description: start_janitor spawns the sweeper thread and returns a JanitorStop that only signals via stop(). If the handle is dropped without calling stop(), rx is closed and try_recv returns Disconnected (not Ok), so the loop keeps running forever and the thread leaks; the loop also only observes the signal at the top of each iteration, delaying shutdown by up to one interval.

findings.title: Issued access tokens are written to stdout
findings.description: issue() prints the full session token with println!("auth: issued token {} for {}", ...). Anyone with read access to logs/process output can steal active bearer tokens and impersonate users.

findings.title: Session tokens are minted from a predictable counter
findings.description: Token generation seeds an LCG with only the current Unix timestamp (seconds) and emits 16 bytes derived from it. An attacker who approximates issuance time can brute-force the small search space and forge bearer tokens.

findings.title: Session expiry is never enforced
findings.description: verify() scans sessions and returns Ok without checking expires_at, so tokens live forever and revoked-by-timeout expectations are bypassed.

findings.title: bearer_token panics on malformed input
findings.description: parts[1] is indexed without a bounds check. An Authorization header without a space (or with only one token) panics the handler thread; a remote client can trigger repeated panics.

findings.title: Password hashing uses a weak, unsalted digest
findings.description: hash_password is a 64-bit djb2-style accumulator with no salt. Passwords can be cracked quickly and identical passwords produce identical hashes.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts a client-supplied header
findings.description: /admin/quotas authorizes based solely on headers.get("x-admin") == "true", ignoring the authenticated session role. Any valid token holder can set the header and read all owners' quotas.

findings.title: delete_link does not enforce ownership
findings.description: Despite the doc comment, delete() removes a link by code for any authenticated user without checking the creator. Any user can delete another user's links (IDOR).

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: out() redirects to the unvalidated next query value, allowing attackers to steer users to arbitrary sites (phishing) and potentially inject headers via CRLF if raw line breaks reach the value.

findings.title: Unknown token is echoed back in the 401 body
findings.description: The 401 response includes the submitted token, which can leak bearer tokens into logs/responses and aids reflection.

findings.title: Permissive CORS with credentials
findings.description: Responses send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, an unsafe permissive configuration for an authenticated API.

findings.title: User-controlled target is emitted unescaped in JSON
findings.description: create_link formats link.target directly into a JSON string. A target containing quotes or control characters can break JSON parsing or lead to stored injection when consumed by browsers/clients.

findings.title: Path traversal via report name
findings.description: export_csv joins dir with format!("{}.csv", name) without sanitizing name. A name like "../../etc/cron.d/x" writes outside export_dir, allowing arbitrary file overwrite by any authenticated user.

findings.title: Path traversal via owner value
findings.description: archive_all builds the output path from the owner key (format!("{}.csv", owner)), so a malicious owner name can escape the export directory and overwrite arbitrary files.

findings.title: CSV fields are not escaped
findings.description: Link fields (code,target,owner,hits) are written verbatim with commas. Values containing commas/newlines can corrupt reports and enable CSV injection (formula injection) when opened in spreadsheets.

findings.title: Panic when creating a link for a new owner
findings.description: create() does self.quota.get_mut(owner).unwrap() without ensuring an entry exists, so the first link for any owner panics the handler thread and can be triggered remotely by any authenticated user.

findings.title: Expired links still resolve due to inverted comparison
findings.description: resolve() sets expired = now < expires_at, the opposite of correct. It removes/returns None for valid links and leaves expired links resolvable, allowing dead codes to be followed and stats inflated.

findings.title: by_owner leaks cross-owner links via substring match
findings.description: Filtering uses l.owner.contains(owner) instead of equality, so querying owner "a" returns links owned by "alice", "bobA", etc. This exposes other owners' link records.

findings.title: extend() resurrects expired links
findings.description: extend() overwrites expires_at even for already-expired links, contradicting the documented invariant that expiry is final and dead codes never come back to life.

findings.title: rename() fails to validate the destination code
findings.description: validate_code is called on `from` twice and never on `to`, so a link can be renamed to an overlong/invalid code, bypassing code validation and degrading integrity.
